en.label: English（原文）
en.summary: Tom Lee and Jay Woods discuss the stock-market rally, lower oil prices and bond yields, technology leadership, weak market breadth, cryptocurrency prices and the approaching midterm elections. The English passages below retain the original transcript and may contain recognition errors.

scenes.title: What triggered the rally? Tom Lee explains the setup for a face ripper
scenes.visual: Tom Lee appears beside an S&P 500 intraday chart showing 7,761.24, up 110.74 (+1.45%). Earlier frames show CNBC's MARKET ALERT and START OF A SEPTEMBER RALLY?, with the Dow up 332.28 (+0.64%) and the Nasdaq Composite up 561.30 (+2.12%).

paragraphs.speaker: Brian
paragraphs.text: Tom Lee, also a CNBC contributor today, certainly is kind of a face ripper, not not just with stocks, with crypto as well. We'll get to that in a minute. Was there a catalyst I missed? What happened?

paragraphs.speaker: Tom Lee
paragraphs.text: You know, Brian, I think last week was maximum pain, maximum pressure because we had a fed hiking very hawkishly and we had high oil prices and rates high.

paragraphs.speaker: Tom Lee
paragraphs.text: And as you know, in the last few days and over the weekend oil cooled and rates are behaving, and now we have a maximum hawkish fed that could walk back and so I think it is all the ingredients for a face ripper, especially given how oversold it is is.

scenes.title: Why lower oil matters: bond yields, inflation and diesel costs

The ticker shows the Dow up 332.28 (+0.64%), the S&P 500 up 111.27 (+1.45%), and the 10-year yield at 4.972%. Earlier frames show WTI October crude around 95.51–95.62, down roughly 4.6%, and a 10-YEAR YIELD BELOW 5% graphic.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian
paragraphs.text: Yeah.
